meta.notes: 9-week post-White River rebuild to Vermont 50K (Sun 9/27: 32-33 mi, ~5,600 ft as 20+ repeated climbs/descents, 37% gravel road, NO POLES). PHASES: W1-2 recovery-dominant (walk/run rebuild, symptom-gated), W3-6 Build, W7 Peak, W8 Taper, W9 Race week. WEEKLY SKELETON (W3+): Mon rest / Tue hill intervals + PM Lower A / Wed easy + upper / Thu easy w-descent block + PM Lower B / Fri easy (longer; absorbs the former Sat shakeout, rev 1.12) + strides or gear-change pickups / Sat REST from running + upper / SUN LONG RUN (moved to Sunday to match race day). Run before strength on every double day; no lower-body strength day-of or day-before the long run. PRIORITY MAP: P1 tendon durability lives in the strength plan and daily routines; P2 hill intervals (pole-free, absorbs runnable-grade economy) from W3; P3 descent capacity gated — Gate 1 (PT assessment) CLEARED pre-plan, gentle exposure from W3, Gate 2 descent-calibration session W5 Thursday clears race-specific volume from W6. INTENSITY DECISION (coach-owned, re-derived rev 1.4): hill intervals Z3-capped per the validated HR-led model; plus short 15-20s uphill strides from W3 — alactic, low-eccentric. STRIDE RATIONALE RE-DERIVED: the original justification cited the +4..8% cadence-collapse finding, RETRACTED 8/6/2026 (Findings Register F-02) — running cadence is 166-178 spm at every grade on all three reference files. Strides are retained on independent grounds: running economy, and the SSC/elastic-tendon demand of Vermont's 20-28 short climb-descent transitions. Strides remain the first thing pulled on any lateral-ankle symptom. No sustained Z4+ work this cycle. GRADE POLICY (new rev 1.4, band-differentiated — replaces the blanket run-everything cue): BELOW +5% run everything, standing instruction, this is where the prize is densest because running's advantage over hiking shrinks as grade rises. +5..8% is a DECLARED TEST ZONE, not an assumed deficit — F-08 is open and the W4 Tuesday test resolves it. ABOVE +8% hike deliberately; Vermont holds only ~5% of its distance above +10%. CADENCE CRITERION (corrected rev 1.4): all climb-rep pass/fail is on run_pct >= 80%, NEVER on a cadence number. Prior cues of 'cadence 130+' and 'cadence 140+' were blend-level figures inherited from walk-contaminated band averages and would pass a half-walked rep. Report cadence_moving_spm alongside. Descent cues moved to median running cadence 175+ to match the analyzer thresholds. TARGET FRAMING (rev 1.4): the training target is ABSOLUTE PACE AT A SUSTAINABLE HR. GAP-parity at grade is NOT a goal and must not be gated on — every climb band on all three reference files already sits at or below a GAP/flat ratio of 1.00 while power hiking, because Minetti is a running model applied outside its domain (Addendum B v4 C-7, Findings Register F-07). FLAT ANCHOR: sustained-block flat running is 10:39-11:00 at peak fitness and 11:18-11:31 detrained. Band averages (11:32 / 13:03) understate the engine and must not be used as targets. LOAD-PATTERN GUARD (June injury lesson): long runs on ROLLING RUNNABLE terrain (100-150 ft/mi, gravel/dirt ideal), never technical-descent mountain routes; min 6 days between long runs; RAMP GUARD (rev 1.2 — rewritten per Race_Strategy_Response_v1 Answers A1/A2/A3). DENOMINATOR: the guard is enforced against SUMMED SESSIONS, never against weekly_targets. weekly_targets.mileage_mi and .vertical_ft are DERIVED fields regenerated from each week's own session sums; they must never be hand-authored, and any loader should assert equality within +/-0.5 mi / +/-50 ft and flag on failure. Rationale: the guard protects tissue, and tissue experiences what is prescribed, not what is summarized. RULES: (1) the W2->W3 step is the recovery-exit rebuild and is exempt from BOTH the percentage and the absolute caps — on session sums it is +9.5 mi / +2,150 ft (14.5 -> 24.0 mi, 300 -> 2,450 ft), roughly double what the old header view (12 -> 19 mi) implied, and it REQUIRES EXPLICIT COACH SIGN-OFF before Week 3 begins; it is not approved by default. (2) absolute caps of +5 mi AND +500 ft apply to any ramp BEGINNING from a week whose session-summed mileage is <=30 mi — the STARTING week is the test. (3) once the starting week exceeds 30 mi the cap is 10%, applied SEPARATELY to mileage and to vertical, each against its own prior-week session sum. (4) any breach pauses the progression at the prior week's volume and flags the coach. COMPLIANCE AT REV 1.2, all on session sums: W3->W4 +5.0 mi / +500 ft (at cap, compliant); W4->W5 +5.0 mi / +500 ft (at cap, compliant); W5->W6 +8.8% mi / +8.7% ft (compliant); W6->W7 +8.1% mi / +9.3% ft (compliant); W7->W8 and W8->W9 both decrease. No breaches. HEADROOM WARNING: the vertical ladder now runs at 87-100% of its ceiling in every build week, and W4 and W5 sit EXACTLY at +500 ft. There is no spare vertical anywhere in W4-W7. Adding gain to any session — including route substitutions that happen to climb more — breaks compliance downstream. The B1 rehearsal spec consumed the last of the headroom; any further vertical request must be funded by an explicit trim elsewhere, not absorbed. W2->W3 EXEMPTION — SETTLED RULE (Run_Plan_rev1_2_Verification_Memo section 3, no longer provisional): the exemption covers BOTH the percentage and the absolute caps. Rationale: the ramp guard is a build-phase instrument, and W2 is a symptom-gated walk/run rebuild whose session sums are not load-comparable to run weeks — walk miles are not run miles — so no arithmetic rule spanning W2->W3 is meaningful in either direction. Governance of that step belongs to the three symptom gates plus the conditional sign-off below, not to the ladder. No re-solve is triggered by this ruling. W2->W3 CONDITIONAL SIGN-OFF (athlete-set, closes the last open human item): the step is PRE-APPROVED AT FULL SIZE (+9.5 mi / +2,150 ft on session sums, 14.5 -> 24.0 mi and 300 -> 2,450 ft) IF AND ONLY IF Weeks 1 and 2 clear all three symptom gates — right lateral ankle, left outer knee, right forefoot — with NO flags. Clean gates means Week 3 starts as written, no further approval needed. ANY flag in W1 or W2 voids the pre-approval, and the ladder re-solves downward with the B1 rehearsal reverting to its 2,600 ft profile (the coupling is stated in the rev 1.2 cover note section 5). Note that a flag severe enough to trigger the existing W1-W2 reset rule is governed by that rule first — reset to the Week 1 Friday level and message the coach — and only then does the reduced-ladder branch apply to whatever Week 3 becomes. LADDER SLACK, computed so the re-solve is not improvised under symptom pressure: holding the 40.0 mi peak week, the W3 floor is 23.06 mi. Against the prescribed 24.0 that is only 0.94 mi of slack — the MILEAGE ladder is effectively rigid, and any meaningful reduction at W3 pulls the peak week down proportionally rather than being absorbed. Vertical is different: the W3 floor is 2,388 ft with the B1 spec intact (62 ft of slack) but 2,058 ft once the rehearsal reverts to 2,600 (392 ft of slack). So the reverted branch buys vertical room and almost no mileage room. Anyone re-solving this ladder should size W3 first, then let W4-W7 fall out of the caps, and expect the peak week to shrink with it; any two of (long run, descent session, steep hill session) never on consecutive days. RECALIBRATION CHECKPOINT W5: Thursday Gate 2 descent session + Sunday rolling calibration long run, both recorded clean and FIT files sent to the Race Strategy project for the Vermont pacing plan v1. Addendum A June-13 tables are CEILINGS from peak fitness — context only, not current targets; the W5 calibration supersedes them. HR ZONES at LTHR 168 — CORRECTED CONTIGUOUS TABLE (per HR_Zone_Gap_Report_v1; orphan bpm values 150/158/167 assigned to their nearest percentage boundary): Z1 Recovery <142 | Z2 Aerobic 142-150 | Z3 Tempo 151-158 | Z4 Sub-threshold 159-167 | Z5a Threshold 168-171. Z5b/c undefined by design — nothing in this program operates there. Nothing operational moves: first-10-mi cap 149 (inside Z2), descent throttle 152 (low Z3), never-cross 158 (now cleanly top of Z3). FIELD CONVENTION: hr_zone = INTENDED EXECUTION BAND (range labels like Z1-2/Z2-3 allowed where intent spans a boundary); hr_cap_bpm = HARD CEILING / alarm value, which may sit above the intended band as a declared tripwire. DOWNSTREAM: whoever parses the Week-5 calibration FIT files (8/27 Gate 2 + 8/30 long run) must bucket HR with these same zone edges (150 in Z2, 158 in Z3) — flag in the parser workflow before processing, not after. SYMPTOM GATES throughout: right lateral-ankle tendon (unproven under load), left outer knee, right forefoot — any recurrence pauses descent work and strides, flags the coach. WEEKLY VERTICAL COMPLIANCE CHECK (added rev 1.3 per verification memo section 4): the Sunday compliance check is extended beyond session completion. Each Sunday, compare ACTUAL GPS-measured weekly vertical against that week's derived weekly_targets.vertical_ft. Because the vertical ladder runs at 87-100% of its ceiling in every build week (W4 and W5 sit exactly at +500 ft), a route substitution that climbs 200 ft over plan is a guard breach, not a rounding difference — the check must catch it the week it happens, not at the next review. Over by more than ~100 ft: the following week's ceiling recomputes off the ACTUAL sum, not the plan, and the coach is messaged. This applies with full force to the two calibration days (8/27 Gate 2 and 8/30 long run), where planned-vs-actual is also checked on the Race Strategy side when the FIT files arrive. VERTICAL COMPOSITION POLICY (rev 1.7, athlete ruling 8/12/2026). The local terrain does not offer routes at the easy-day vertical figures written in this plan: the athlete's default trail loop measures 3.75 mi / 528 ft, i.e. 141 ft/mi, against easy-day prescriptions near 60-100 ft/mi. RULING: vertical is ALLOCATED TO THE LONG RUN, which runs on that loop as the Vermont simulator, and SHAVED FROM OTHER SESSIONS by moving them to road. Rationale, and the precedent: 8/11 came in 146 ft under its 600 ft prescription and still passed every rep criterion, because the approach vertical is not what those sessions are for. THE WEEKLY TOTAL IS HELD BY COMPOSING THE LONG RUN — loop count plus flat filler, giving a 528 ft dial with mileage as the fine adjustment — NOT by trimming quality days. CONSTRAINT THAT TRAVELS WITH THIS RULING: the shaveable budget is roughly 200-250 ft per week, not the apparent easy-day total. Thursday-type descent skill blocks FUND their own vertical (on a loop, descent implies ascent, so flattening deletes the P3 stimulus rather than the vertical); 8/18 is locked and vertical-neutral; W4's 8/20 is descent volume. THE SUNDAY VERTICAL CHECK IS UNCHANGED and still governs — this policy changes how the weekly total is ASSEMBLED, not the guard, the ~100 ft trigger, or the recompute-off-actual rule. If the check fires, it fires. WATCH ITEM: multi-loop long runs concentrate the eccentric dose (two loops is roughly 680 ft of -7% descent in one session) rather than distributing it across the week, so the 24 h symptom response at the three monitored sites carries more weight on the day after a long run than it did under the distributed pattern. P1 gating is unchanged and the technical-descent ban is unchanged; this loop is used on the basis that it is non-technical. TERRAIN INTENT (rev 1.9, 2026-08-18). Every future session carries terrain_intent, which states WHAT THE TERRAIN MUST DELIVER rather than what the terrain is called. VALUES: free (no terrain requirement - HR and duration carry the session); grade (a named grade band must be hit inside the session - THE BAND IS THE POINT AND THE SURFACE IS NOT); relief (cumulative ft/mi is the target); relief+grade (both, with the named block winning any conflict); footing (technical footing is itself the stimulus - DEFINED BUT NEVER ASSIGNED in this plan, because the technical-descent ban is active for the whole cycle; it exists so that its absence is visible rather than assumed). TERRAIN_INTENT GOVERNS AND terrain IS NOW ADVISORY, retained for provenance only. Where the two disagree - and they do, because several grade sessions still read terrain trail - terrain_intent wins. Stated explicitly because two fields asserting one quantity with nothing saying which is authoritative is the defect class behind PC-4 and the inverted block GAP. AN ABSENT terrain_intent MEANS UNCLASSIFIED, NEVER free: Weeks 1-3 and race day carry no value by design, and silently defaulting an absent field to a permissive value is how a guard stops guarding. NON-TECHNICAL FOOTING IS MANDATORY ON EVERY SESSION REGARDLESS OF INTENT and is therefore NOT an enum value - the technical-descent ban (Findings Register F-10) is not a terrain preference, it is the load-pattern guard. SURFACE PREFERENCE ON grade SESSIONS, in order: gravel road, dirt road, smooth trail, pavement. Pavement is last only because it is 5% of the race, not because it trains worse; Vermont is 37% gravel road and 58% trail/jeep road, so a graded road block is MORE course-specific than singletrack, not less. WHY THIS EXISTS: rolling trail cannot hold a stable grade - grade SD inside a running block runs about 4.1 points on trail and 6.08 on the athlete's default loop - so a card naming both a tight band and trail asks for two things local terrain cannot supply together. This resolves that by saying which one is the session. SUBSTITUTION GUIDANCE lives in Terrain_Substitution_Rules_v1.md and is not restated here.

exercises.name: Walking knee hugs
exercises.cue: Pull knee to chest, balance on standing leg for 1 second.

exercises.name: Leg swings — front/back
exercises.cue: Hold something for balance; relaxed, full range.

exercises.name: Leg swings — side/side
exercises.cue: Open the hip, don't twist the spine.

exercises.name: Walking lunges
exercises.cue: Front knee tracks over second toe; keep torso tall.

exercises.name: Glute bridges
exercises.cue: Squeeze glutes at the top; ribs down.

exercises.name: High knees
exercises.cue: Quick turnover; emphasize lift, not speed.

exercises.name: Strides (quality days only)
exercises.cue: Build to ~85% of 5K pace over 20 sec. 60 sec full recovery between. Skip on easy days.

pre_run.notes: Do this BEFORE every run. On easy/shakeout days, omit strides. On quality days (hill intervals, race-rhythm sessions), include the 3 x strides. During recovery weeks 1-2, do the mobility items only, gently.

exercises.name: Walking cooldown
exercises.cue: Walk until HR is below 110 bpm before stretching.

exercises.name: Standing quad stretch
exercises.cue: Tuck pelvis under to feel the stretch in the front of the hip too.

exercises.name: Standing calf stretch (bent + straight knee)
exercises.cue: Two angles per side: knee straight (gastroc) and knee bent (soleus).

exercises.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
exercises.cue: Squeeze the back glute first, THEN lean forward.

exercises.name: Pigeon stretch
exercises.cue: Square hips. If knee complains, lie back instead (figure-4 supine).

exercises.name: Foam roll quads, IT band, calves (optional)
exercises.cue: 60 seconds per area; pause and breathe on tender spots.

post_run.notes: Do within 15 minutes of finishing the run. Especially important after long runs and power-climb days — eccentric load + walking cooldown protects the quads.

weekly_targets.notes: Recovery week 1 of 2. Walking only until Friday; first jog steps are symptom-gated. Mileage figure counts jogged minutes only. SYMPTOM GATE all week: any sharp or localized pain in the right lateral ankle, left outer knee, or right forefoot ends the session and pushes the progression back 2 days.
weekly_targets.derivation_rule: DERIVED FIELD — regenerated from this week's session sums (race excluded). Never hand-author. Loaders should assert mileage_mi and vertical_ft equal the session sums within +/-0.5 mi / +/-50 ft and flag on failure. W1 EXCEPTION: Week 1 sessions are duration-prescribed walk/jog with no distance or vertical values, so the derived header is 0 by construction. Actual content is ~175 min of walking with ~14 min of jogged intervals. The pre-rev-1.2 header of "3 mi" was a hand-authored estimate of jogged minutes and has been removed rather than fabricated back. LOADER CONVENTION: a session omitting elevation_gain_ft or distance_mi is treated as 0; as of rev 1.3 all such fields are written explicitly, so an absent field now indicates a malformed record rather than a zero.

weeks.week_notes: Days 2-8 post-White River. The job this week is circulation and tissue protection, not fitness. Elevation and gentle walking early; short jog intervals only from Friday, only if walking is fully comfortable. No NSAIDs around any loading (blunts collagen remodeling). Strength plan carries the P1 tendon-entry work (isometrics, no HSR).

days.day_notes: Full rest. Short walks around the house, elevation when sitting, pre-stand mobility. Day 2 post-race.

sessions.title: Recovery walk
sessions.key_cue: Flat, supportive shoes, conversational stroll. This is circulation, not training.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. Walk only. Note how the right lateral ankle and left knee feel at the start vs. end — this is baseline data for the week.

sessions.title: Recovery walk
sessions.key_cue: Slightly longer. Still flat. Stop early without guilt if anything localizes.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. Tendon-entry strength session this evening (see strength plan) — isometrics only.

days.day_notes: Rest from walking volume. Daily routines + evening isometrics only. Assess: is walking symptom-free? That answer gates Friday.

sessions.title: Walk + first jog steps (gated)
sessions.key_cue: 6 x 1 min VERY easy jog inside a 45-min walk — ONLY if walking has been fully symptom-free since Wednesday.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. Day 6 post-race. If any of the three sites (right lateral ankle, left outer knee, right forefoot) speaks up on the jog steps, drop back to walking and retry Sunday.

days.day_notes: Rest or optional 25-30 min flat walk. Flex day — listen to the legs.

sessions.title: Long walk + jog intervals

sessions.title: GRADE-ECONOMY TEST (F-08) + reduced hill reps
sessions.key_cue: ROAD CLIMB (Garmin course 499037395, scouted). CONTINUOUS LAPPING — press lap at EVERY transition so work and recovery alternate with no un-lapped time. Auto-lap OFF. L1 flat reference 6 min steady running on the 1% terrain. L2 block A climb 0.00-0.50 @ +5.0%. L3 recovery, walk 0.25 down and 0.25 back up, settle 60-90 s at the 0.50 mark before pressing. L4 block B climb 0.50-1.00 @ +8.5%. L5 recovery, walk down to base. L6 block C repeat 0.00-0.50 @ +5.0%. L7 walk down. L8 4 x 20 s strides. RUN EVERY BLOCK TO COMPLETION at steady running effort — do NOT pace to a cap and do not walk. 157 is an ABORT tripwire, not a target. WALK the recoveries, do not jog them — a jogged recovery lets PC-1 merge block-recovery-block into one running stream with grade floating; walking segments the blocks for free. This changes the parse, not only the load.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Quality / MEASUREMENT. This is the Addendum C s9 test and it is the highest-value measurement in the block (Findings Register F-08). THE QUESTION: running continuously at grade, does HR plateau below the ceiling or rise monotonically until you are forced to walk? Plateau -> P2 becomes volume and execution rehearsal. Monotonic rise -> P2 becomes economy work and Lever C (the ceiling itself) moves to the front. TERRAIN FIELD CORRECTED rev 1.4a: was 'trail', which contradicted the cue. Rolling trail cannot produce a stable continuous grade — grade SD within running blocks averages 4.1 percentage points, which is what defeated the v7 iso-HR rule in the first place. This session REQUIRES a road or graded fireroad climb. PROTOCOL NOTE: turn OFF auto-lap so manual lap presses are the only block boundaries (Parser spec PC-2). READ-OUT REQUIRED: HR start/end/max and slope in bpm/min within each block, pace, cadence_moving_spm, run_pct, and % of seconds above cap — not block averages. HEAT GATE (convention C-2): coolest available window. Heat index above 85 F invalidates the HR read entirely — if the forecast breaches it, the session SLIPS TO W5 TUESDAY 8/25 and the hill reps run as originally written. The test must precede the 8/27 Gate 2 and 8/30 calibration package. P1 INTERACTION: uphill running is concentric-dominant and race climbing was pain-free, so this is tendon-compatible; confirm the three symptom sites are clear before starting. VERTICAL-NEUTRAL: 800 ft total is UNCHANGED from rev 1.3 — the test blocks are funded by reducing approach and recovery climbing, not by adding gain. W4 sits exactly at the +500 ft ramp cap and has no headroom. COURSE LOCKED rev 1.4b: Garmin course 499037395, road. Measured profile — 1.245 mi, 422 ft, continuous ascent. Block A mi 0.00-0.50 mean +5.0%, grade SD 1.3 pts. Block B mi 0.50-1.00 mean +8.5%, grade SD 0.9 pts. Separation 3.5 percentage points. CUT AT 0.50 (rev 1.4c), replacing an earlier 0.55 offset — same grade quality, cleaner boundary, and 19 ft cheaper on the approach re-climb. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: 'rest of ascent' mi 0.50-1.245 averages +7.3%, closer to the original +6..7% target, but grade SD doubles to 2.3 pts because the road crests — per-0.1-mi it runs 8.4, 8.3, 8.9, 9.4, 7.5, 7.6, 3.5, 2.8. That average is a steep-plus-flat blend, the same class of artifact as a walk-contaminated band mean. A block whose grade shifts six points partway cannot answer a stable-grade HR question. Trail comparison SD is 4.1 pts, so this road delivers the grade stability the test requires. DESIGN NOTE: the two blocks BRACKET the +5..8% test zone rather than sampling inside it. Both plateau -> the whole zone is runnable. A plateaus and B does not -> the boundary sits inside the zone, interpolate. Neither plateaus -> the boundary is below +5% and P2 reshapes substantially. A pass at +5.0% generalises downward to +3..4%, so the gentle end is covered. Block B at +8.6% is above the rev 1.4 hike line; 'could not run it' is a valid and informative result there. SECOND GENTLE BLOCK RESTORED (rev 1.4d). An earlier draft cut it on budget grounds, using a descend-to-base plus jog-up recovery costing 1.00 mi and 133 ft of re-climb. Athlete proposed walking 0.25 down and 0.25 back up instead — same recovery effect at half the distance and ~60 ft less climbing, and walking descent recovers better than jogging. That saving funds block C. Planned total 4.55 mi / 562 ft against 4.5 / 800. BLOCK C VALUE: repeating +5.0% after block B and a mile of descending is a within-session check on whether the same grade costs more under accumulated work — a cheap partial read on the fatigue question Addendum B v4 s11 withdrew, and the closest approximation to race conditions in the session. First thing dropped if the right lateral ankle responds on the walk-downs. DESCENT LOAD: 1.75 mi of descending, all easy-paced recovery rather than descent work, on a day carrying Lower A in the evening. Keep every descent genuinely easy. FLAT REFERENCE: 1% terrain at the base, confirmed available. Use the longest continuous straight or the widest loop — tight loops depress flat pace through braking and acceleration, which would bias BOTH climb comparisons favourably and corrupt the anchor the whole test rests on. If the loop is tight, note it and the flat figure is treated as a floor rather than a value. FLAT REFERENCE CONFIRMED (athlete, 2026-08-10): 1% terrain available at the base for the reference block. Route starts at 5 ft elevation. DATA CAVEAT: Garmin course elevation is DEM-derived at ~27 m point spacing; real road may undulate slightly more than the profile shows. DURATION CHANGED rev 1.4e: 50 -> 70 min. THIS IS A LOAD-FIELD CHANGE and the only one in rev 1.4; distance_mi and elevation_gain_ft remain untouched across the whole revision. Driver is 2.0 mi of recovery walking at ~15-20 min/mi, roughly 30-35 min on its own. Work blocks total ~28 min. The ramp guard governs mileage and vertical, not duration, so weekly compliance is unaffected; walking recovery carries near-zero physiological load. Consequences that DO matter: greater heat exposure, which makes the coolest-window instruction and the 85 F gate more binding, and a longer gap needed before Lower A. BLOCKS ARE DISTANCE-DEFINED, NOT TIME-DEFINED (changed from the original 6-min spec): a physical landmark is a more reliable lap boundary than a timer and keeps each block's grade matched to the measured road segment. Expected durations: L1 6:00 time-capped, L2 6:15-7:30, L4 7:15-9:00, L6 6:30-7:45. Longer than 6 min is an improvement — plateau vs monotonic rise reads more clearly over 8 min. If block B turns into a hike partway, STOP the block there, press lap, and note the distance. That is a result, not a failed session. STRIDES moved from hill to flat (logistics — avoids re-climbing); the session already carries 490 ft of climbing so the climbing-specific stimulus is covered. FLAT REFERENCE TARGET: let HR settle at 140-145, ideally ~142, and let pace be the output. Do NOT set a pace target — fixing pace on the flat fixes the wrong variable and biases both climb comparisons. Expect roughly 11:00-11:30/mi. Carry the same perceived effort into block A. Lower A this evening as scheduled, with adequate gap. READ-OUT ADDITION (rev 1.5, Dispositions s3): report the steep block BOTH uncorrected AND decay-corrected. Estimate time decay linearly between the BLOCK A and BLOCK C midpoints (both +5.0%) and interpolate MULTIPLICATIVELY to BLOCK B — the 8/9 session showed decay as a proportional penalty on a common pace scale (16.1-16.7% across three non-climbing grade bins), not an additive grade term. STATE that the A->C slope contains any fatigue BLOCK B itself induced, so the correction is an UPPER BOUND on decay and the corrected figures are optimistic. The read must hold across BOTH bounds or the session did not settle it. DECLARED ASSUMPTION: the 8/9 climbing bin (+3..+6%) ran 19.8% against 16.1-16.7% for the three non-climbing bins — about 3 points clear on 166 late seconds. If decay RATE differs between +5.0% and +8.5%, the multiplicative interpolation to BLOCK B carries an additional unquantified error. Small sample, stated as an assumption rather than discovered in the read-out. BLOCK NAMING RECONCILED rev 1.5: the disposition was written against the retired 4-block design (BLOCK 2/4 at +3..4%, BLOCK 3 at +6..7%); it maps onto the locked course as A/C and B respectively. Method unchanged. READ-OUT ADDITION (rev 1.6, Rulings 20260810 s3): report WITHIN-BLOCK HR SLOPE in bpm/min for BLOCK A, BLOCK B and BLOCK C SEPARATELY. This is a free falsification test of the residual assumption above and needs no change to the session. If the climbing bin genuinely carries a grade-dependent decay term, BLOCK B's within-block slope should EXCEED both BLOCK A's and BLOCK C's. If all three are comparable, the 19.8% separation is more likely a small-sample artifact of 166 seconds and the multiplicative interpolation is safe. RESIDUAL STATED PRECISELY, so it is falsifiable rather than merely disclosed: the risk is NOT 'decay might behave differently on climbs', it is 'the decay RATE may differ between +5.0% and +8.5%, in which case multiplicative interpolation from BLOCK A and BLOCK C to BLOCK B carries an unquantified error ON TOP OF the fatigue-contamination bound.' Block names remapped from the ruling's retired BLOCK 2/3/4 exactly as in rev 1.5; method unchanged.

Recording it is what makes the within-block HR slope readable anyway. Nothing about the effort changes on the day.

THE 8/18 CARD EQUALISED THE GRADE AND LEFT THE RECOVERY MODE FREE; that is the design gap. TWO FIXES EXIST AND THIS CARD TAKES THE SECOND: (a) equalise recovery across reps, which WOULD CHANGE THE STIMULUS here because back-to-back pairs are the Vermont transition rhythm this session exists to train, or (b) leave the recovery asymmetric and RECORD THE ENTRY STATE so the slope means one thing across all six reps. sessions.key_cue: ROUTE (rev 1.11): Perkins Memorial Drive, START AT THE SUMMIT. Long side = 3.0 mi / 900 ft at 5.7% avg (top 0.4 mi 8-9%, middle 1.5 mi 3-5%, bottom 0.4 mi 5-8%). Short side = 1.37 mi / 370 ft at 5.3% avg. Paved, all descending under 10%. Source GPX: Perking_Memorial.gpx, parsed gpx_parser_05282026 (5 m grid, W=15). SEQUENCE ~20.7 mi / ~2,950 ft / ~4.5 h: [0-0.5] easy jog on the summit loop, settle HR. [0.5-3.2] short side down, short side up (warm-up pair, cap 149). [3.2-9.2] long side down, long side up. Hours 0-2 end about here. [9.2-12.0] short side down, short side up (RUN). [12.0-13.4] short side down. [13.4-14.8] HIKE ARM: short side up, deliberate pole-free hike the whole 1.37 mi, LAP-PRESS AT BOTH ENDS. [14.8-17.8] D3 REHEARSAL: long side down, 3.0 mi continuous at -5.7% - the mi 25.0-29.5 analogue. [17.8-20.7] RUN ARM: turn at the bottom WITHOUT STOPPING and run the long side up, finishing at the summit. The first 1.4 mi (+376 ft at 5.1%) is the mi 29.5-30.9 analogue: run it at drifted HR, LOW Z3 PERMITTED, tripwire 156. Above that the run/hike rule governs as normal; the upper 0.4 mi at 8-9% is where it will bite. LAP-PRESS at the turn and at 1.4 mi. CEILING SCHEDULE (rev 1.11, replaces the flat 149 cap): hours 0-2 cap 149; thereafter ~+3 bpm/hr drift allowance on flat and descent bands; HARD TRIPWIRE 156 all day; CLIMB ENTRY GATE 140-145 enforced all day - walk/settle before a climb starts, not after. Time over 149 is reported informationally, not as a deviation. CAFFEINE GEL around mi 14 so it lands 15-20 min before the final climb. READ-OUT: hike arm and run arm on the F-08 template (pace, HR start/end/max, slope bpm/min, running-only cadence, % seconds above cap), plus for the run arm: did the run hold, finishing HR, time to recover under 145 after the summit, and the hike-vs-run HR delta at matched grade. Hours 4+ fueling and HR decay are the other required outputs.

S6 (6-min hiking block) becomes the Lever C paired gait test: hike arm 1.37 mi at 5.3% vs run arm 1.4 mi at 5.1%, matched length and grade, both in the final hour. S4 day total ~2,950 ft (~140 ft/mi) and S5 caffeine timing carry. MECHANISM ON RECORD (RS memo s2): the 8/30 late +5..10% run-share collapse was HR-governed under drift, not leg failure; run-vs-hike on late moderate climbs is an open ceiling question this session tests, not a capacity gap. STEEP DESCENT SAMPLING (RS ask d, >=3 min at <=-10%) DECLINED by athlete 8/31: it would breach the <10% route constraint; the route holds nothing near -10%. LOAD DELTA vs rev 1.10: +0.7 mi, -50 ft, +30 min; week 7 derived targets regenerated from sums. Rehearses the whole race day: rehearsed breakfast, race vest, race shoes, race fueling cadence, run-everything execution. SPEC SOURCE: Race_Strategy_Response_v1 Answer B1 — the spec is a DISTRIBUTION, not an average; 130 ft/mi was never the problem and 172 was never the answer. ROUTE CONSTRAINT (non-negotiable): all added or steepened descent must be runnable (<10%); the technical-descent ban stands. Added climbing on a loop means added descending — route selection must absorb it at runnable grades. GATE CONDITION: this spec is conditional on Gate 2 (8/27) passing unflagged AND the 8/30 calibration reading clean. If either flags, this session REVERTS to 20 mi / 2,600 ft / 130 ft/mi and the spec is dropped without discussion — a gentler rehearsal is a smaller loss than a re-injury six days before taper. The revert is also guard-safe: 3,700 ft for the week is a decrease from W6. HIKING BLOCK RATIONALE (rev 1.5): the only sustained pole-free hiking data on this athlete comes from WR50K at 5,600-5,900 ft in a detrained state, race hours 4.9-6.9. Both bias that arm SLOW, i.e. conservatively toward running. This block measures it in current trained state at Vermont-like altitude and late-race fatigue, inside a session already on the calendar. The standalone W5 calibration was DECLINED (Dispositions s6) — the 8/25 slip window stays available as the 8/18 heat fallback and its hill-interval session is UNCHANGED. RUN/HIKE DECISION RULE (rev 1.6, Rulings 20260810 s4) — REHEARSE THIS, it is the rule for race day. 1. HR CAP GOVERNS. ALWAYS. [constraint] 2. Running pace at or under ~18:00/mi -> KEEP RUNNING. [PACE] 3. Running pace at or over ~18:00/mi -> HIKE. [PACE] 4. LATE IN THE RACE, SWITCH EARLIER THAN RULE 3 SAYS. [DAMAGE] RULE 4 OVERRIDES RULE 3 — it does not extend it. Stated plainly because the two rest on DIFFERENT AXES AND POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS at exactly the point the decision matters most, the mi 29.4 climb. On PACE alone the threshold LOOSENS late: hiking slows by roughly 1:46/mi within a long effort, so running keeps winning longer, and rule 3 by itself would say run MORE late in the race. Rule 4 resolves toward TISSUE COST, not pace, because the documented failure mode is structural — WR descent HR 136-141 in deep Z1 with pace 2-3 min/mi off plan. The pace argument is worth about a minute on one late climb; the damage argument governs every descending mile after it. NOTE: the ~18:00 threshold is grade-dependent in reality (pole-free sustained hiking is 16:55/mi at +3.5% and 18:08/mi at +6.5%), so at gentle grades the flat threshold switches slightly late. Immaterial while rule 1 binds.
